result:
I reviewed the frontend unit test suite and coverage. Summary:

## Test command
```
npx nx test frontend --code-coverage
```
The `--code-coverage` flag isn't set by default in `apps/frontend/project.json`, so I added it for this run.

## Result: ✅ All tests pass
7 test suites, 88 tests — all passed. (Some `console.error` noise from jsdom/Chart.js canvas fallback in `group-chart.component.spec.ts` — not test failures.)

## Coverage highlights
- **Overall**: 91.18% statements / 100% branches / 87.23% functions / 90.14% lines
- 100% across the board for: `group-chart`, `neighborhood-monthly-chart`, `results-table`, `search`, `neighborhoods.ts` constants, and `csb-requests.service.ts`
- **Biggest gap**: `monthly-chart.component.ts` — 36.84% stmts / 0% functions / 29.41% lines. There's no spec file for this component at all, so `ngOnInit()` (both success and error subscribe paths) is completely untested.
- `app.ts` lines 52–53 uncovered — the error-handling branch in `fetchResults()` isn't tested.
- `app.config.ts` / `app.routes.ts` at 0% — currently trivial/declarative, lower priority, but flagged since the roadmap mentions upcoming routing/chart work.

Note: no `coverage-summary.json` was produced (Jest config lacks the `json-summary` reporter), so I sourced the per-file metrics from the console coverage table/`coverage-final.json` instead — flagged in the report as a config suggestion.

Full report written to: `coverage-reports/2026-09-01-coverage-report.md`

tool_input.command: find /workspace/coverage/apps/frontend -iname "coverage-summary.json"; echo ---; cat /workspace/coverage/apps/frontend/coverage-summary.json 2>/dev/null | python3 -m json.tool | head -300
